facts.claim: A marriage licence for a foreign national legally residing in Greece is issued by the competent department of the municipality of residence; the competent body for the procedure is the Ministry of Interior.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Residents of Greece only. Not the route for couples living in the UK.

facts.claim: 'The mayor or the president of the community shall wait for one week from the date of submission of the relevant application for any possible objection by third parties.' Deadline of completion: 7 days; the licence is granted immediately after expiry of the one-week period if there is no objection.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Resident route. See F-15 (8 days end to end on the civil-licence entry).

facts.claim: The clock starts on the date the application is submitted; staff check all documents and the newspaper notice, then issue a protocol number. Incomplete applications are returned and the procedure starts again.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Fee for issuing the licence to a foreign resident: EUR 18, paid as an e-paravolo (code 2386).
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Resident licence only. The civil-licence entry for residents (F-15) says 'provided without cost'.

facts.claim: The licence is valid for 6 months.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Documents for the foreign-resident licence include a certificate of no impediment from the competent consular or other authority, a birth certificate translated into Greek, proof of residence, passport or residence permit, a translated divorce decree if relevant, and the newspaper issue carrying the marriage announcement.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Documents from Hague Convention countries are accepted only with an Apostille and 'translated into Greek by a Greek translator'.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: UK apostilles come from the FCDO Legalisation Office (see UK facts).

facts.claim: Legal basis: Civil Code articles 1368 to 1370; Law 1250/1982 (civil marriage); PD 391/1982; Law 5089/2024 (marriage between persons of the same sex).
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Athens Civil Marriages Department serves permanent residents of the City of Athens and Greek citizens abroad registered in Athens; applicants appear in person with ID. 'The marriage license is issued seven (7) days after the submission and verification of the required documents and is valid for six (6) months.'
facts.use_note: Athens publishes no route for foreigners living abroad.

facts.claim: Athens: every document lodged must have been issued within the last six months; a home-country marital status certificate must have been issued within the last three months. Foreign residents need a home-country marriage licence with Apostille, or a Certificate of No Impediment from the home country or its Embassy in Greece, officially authenticated and translated into Greek, plus an authenticated, translated birth certificate.

Whether you can get married abroad depends on local laws. You need to check the laws in the country where you want to marry, find out the process, and check which documents you need to prove you are free to marry. You can get advice from the person conducting the ceremony, the authority that registers marriages in that country, or a wedding planner.
facts.use_note: gov.uk/marriage-abroad/y/greece now redirects to this generic guide; there is no longer a Greece-specific gov.uk marriage page.

facts.claim: Some countries may ask for documents to prove you are free to marry, for example a certificate of no impediment or a marital status affirmation. The gov.uk online service lets you check which documents you might need and apply and pay for them. You must have a valid British passport to use this service. Once started, an application cannot be saved and times out after 30 minutes of inactivity.
facts.use_note: Online service: prove-eligibility-foreign-government.service.gov.uk. The guide does not name the document Greece requires or its fee; see gaps.

facts.claim: When you marry abroad, the authorities in that country register it in their national civil records. 'You cannot get a UK marriage or civil partnership certificate if your marriage or civil partnership happened abroad. Only UK marriages and civil partnerships are registered in the UK.'
facts.use_note: Key correction for UK readers: there is no UK registration of a Greek marriage. Keep the Greek certificate.

facts.claim: A foreign marriage is recognised in the UK if it was lawful in the country where it took place and it would be allowed under UK law. You may want to get your foreign certificate translated, which can help if you plan to use it outside the country where it was issued. If you want a UK marriage certificate, you can choose a legal ceremony in the UK and a commitment ceremony abroad.

FCDO entry requirements for Greece (full 'British citizen' passport): Greece follows Schengen rules. The passport must have a date of issue less than 10 years before the date you arrive, and an expiry date at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area. You can travel without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period as a tourist or to visit family or friends.
facts.use_note: The travel advice has no wedding-specific notes. It says to contact the Greek Embassy in the UK if unsure how entry rules apply. Watch the 10-year issue date rule for older passports.

facts.claim: The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) is being implemented across Schengen; Greek authorities have indicated that they will not collect biometric data (fingerprints and photos) for UK travellers as part of EES.
facts.use_note: Optional travel note. Can change; recheck before publishing.

facts.claim: The FCDO Legalisation Office legalises UK public documents (for example a birth, marriage or death certificate from a public registry, or documents certified by a UK notary or solicitor) by attaching an apostille. It cannot legalise documents issued outside the UK. Birth, marriage and other General Register Office certificates cannot get an e-Apostille; they need a paper-based apostille.
facts.source_date: page shows dateModified 2015-02-25; fees live on 2026-11-20
facts.use_note: So a UK birth certificate for Greece needs a paper apostille.

facts.claim: Legalisation fees per document: Standard (paper-based) GBP 45 plus courier or postage; e-Apostille GBP 35. Courier return within the UK GBP 6 per 1.5kg. Standard service usually takes up to 25 working days plus courier or postage time; e-Apostille up to 2 working days.
facts.use_note: Write as GBP 45 per document (paper). Up to 25 working days is the main timing risk for UK couples.

facts.claim: FCDO consular fee 11: 'Issuing a certificate that no impediment to an intended marriage or civil partnership has been shown to exist, or issuing any local equivalent document for an intended marriage ... in accordance with local law': GBP 50 (in English or any other language). Fee 10, receiving notice of an intended marriage: GBP 50. Fees are charged in British pounds and are the same in every country.
facts.use_note: Medium: this is the general consular fee schedule. Which document Greece needs from a UK resident (CNI, or another document) and the total charged by the online service are shown only inside the application flow, which could not be read. Say 'the FCDO consular fee for a CNI or local equivalent is GBP 50 per document' and confirm the Greece outcome in the gov.uk service.

facts.claim: HM Passport Office: you can get a new passport in your new name before or after the ceremony. After the ceremony, send your marriage certificate when you apply in your new name (including double-barrelled names). Online application costs GBP 102; paper costs GBP 115.50. You do not need a new passport if you marry but keep your name. The name on your passport must match the one you use when you book travel.
facts.use_note: Book flights to Greece in your current passport name.

facts.claim: You can apply for a passport in your new name up to 3 months before the ceremony; the new passport is post-dated and cannot be used before the ceremony, and your old one is cancelled. You must send a 'passports for newly weds and civil partners' form signed by the religious minister or registrar who will conduct the ceremony. Some countries will not issue visas for post-dated passports.
facts.use_note: Do not recommend this for a Greek wedding: you would travel on a passport not valid until the ceremony, and the form must be signed by the Greek officiant. Whether that works abroad is not stated. Advise changing name after the wedding.

facts.claim: A foreign marriage certificate is a non-UK document: the FCDO Legalisation Office cannot legalise documents issued outside the UK; they must be legalised in the country where they were issued.
facts.use_note: If a UK body wants a Greek certificate apostilled, that apostille comes from Greece. Which Greek authority issues it is a gap.
